structure: Part 1 (Version mount, layout and journey control), read at commit 04a073b (the checkout's HEAD). Read in full: app/lib/version-mount.js (363 lines: shared session keys, the 34 journey path prefixes, shared external paths, path prefixing for redirects and render data, the separate session nest, view-override fallback, router copying), app/lib/design-release-2.1-version.js (42 lines: base path /design-release-2.1, session key _designRelease21, flag _isDesignRelease21Version, locals including the four service-navigation hrefs), app/filters.js (10 lines, no filters) and app/data/session-data-defaults.js (5 lines, no defaults); layouts/main.html (header and the four service-navigation variants), layouts/journey.html (two-thirds column and the cancel-amend modal include), index.html (the prototype index with four release cards); partials/design-release-2.1/journey-form-actions.html (three action modes: template review, amend, default), partials/notification-status.html and partials/design-release-2.1/notification-status.html (status tag and reference, Cancel amend link), partials/design-release-2/cancel-amend-modal.html. app/routes.js ranges: 1-67 (requires and constants, including the design-release reference GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P), 273-401 (notification reference helpers, resetNotificationJourneySession, seedPrototypeSessionForReasonForImport), 436-499 (from-hub, from-review, from-template-review, template-review return and save, getJourneyBackLink), 1495-1603 (getJourneySteps, getNextJourneyPath, amend detection, form action parsing, getJourneySaveRedirect, getSectionContinueRedirect), 7052-7106 (design release base path, address book href, dashboard back link), 11720-11723 (GET /index), 13103-13114 (POST /intro/sign-in and the version mounting order). To state step conditions accurately, the bodies of the helpers getJourneySteps calls (hasAnimalIdentifiersRequired, requiresAdditionalAnimalDetailsPage, requiresTransitCountries, isDesignRelease21TemplateCreate) and generateDesignReleaseNotificationReference were looked up in other parts' ranges and cited, not claimed in their own right. Claims cover the mount and session model, link prefixing, view fallback, service navigation and header, the index page, the journey layout, form actions, notification status, cancel-amend modal, notification references, session reset, prototype seeding, back links and return rules, the step order with every conditional step, next-page logic, save redirects, the sign-in redirect, GET /index and the mount order.

claims.statement: Design release 2.1 is served under the base path /design-release-2.1.

Every route of the root router is copied under /design-release-2.1 (each method of each route, with the same handlers), so DR2.1 has the same pages and handlers as the root journey rather than its own route table.
The versions are mounted in the order testing, design release 2.1, design release 2; 2.1 is mounted before 2 so that /design-release-2.1 is not taken as a /design-release-2 path.

Under /design-release-2.1 the session data a page sees is a separate nest stored under the session key _designRelease21, so DR2.1 notifications, drafts and answers are kept apart from the root journey and the other versions.
Inside the DR2.1 session nest the flag _isDesignRelease21Version is set to true on every request, which handlers use to tell they are running as DR2.1.

Two session keys are shared across all versions rather than kept in the DR2.1 nest: the addresses added to the address book (addressBookAddedAddresses) and the submitted notifications (submittedNotifications). Reading or writing them in DR2.1 reads or writes the shared value.

When a DR2.1 request carries a form or query field (not starting with an underscore, not the session key and not a shared key) whose name also exists in the shared session outside the DR2.1 nest, the nest takes the outer session's value for that key before the handler runs.
claims.note: This copies the outer session's value into the nest; the posted value itself is applied later by the prototype kit. Recorded as observed, not interpreted further.

claims.statement: Before a DR2.1 response redirects or ends, the session is restored so the DR2.1 nest is saved back under _designRelease21 in the full session.

In DR2.1, a redirect to a journey path is prefixed with /design-release-2.1 (for example a redirect to /notification-hub goes to /design-release-2.1/notification-hub), and a redirect to / goes to /design-release-2.1.

In DR2.1, every string in the data passed to a page render that is a journey path is prefixed with /design-release-2.1, so links, form actions and back links built by handlers stay inside the version.

The journey path prefixes that are kept inside the version are: /create-notification, /notification-type, /origin-of-the-import, /what-are-you-importing, /reason-for-import, /consignment-details, /animal-identification-details, /additional-animal-details, /arrival-details, /transit-countries, /transporter, /upload-documents, /roles-and-addresses, /place-of-origin, /consignor-or-exporter, /consignee, /importer, /place-of-destination, /cph-number, /permanent-address, /contact-address-for-consignment, /review-notification, /declaration, /notification-submitted, /notification-hub, /notifications, /dashboard, /live-animals, /germinal-products, /templates, /actions, /changes, /inspection and /prototype/reason-for-import (each path itself or anything below it).
Paths that are not journey paths are left unprefixed: external or protocol-relative links, links not starting with /, fragment links starting with #, and any path not in the journey prefix list.

The address book (/address-book and anything below it), static assets (/public/, /plugin-assets/), the prototype kit management pages (/manage-prototype) and the service index (/index) are shared paths that are never prefixed with the version base path.
claims.quote:
return urlPath === '/address-book' ||
    urlPath.startsWith('/address-book/') ||
    urlPath.startsWith('/public/') ||
    urlPath.startsWith('/plugin-assets/') ||
    urlPath.startsWith('/manage-prototype') ||
    urlPath === '/index'

claims.statement: A path that already starts with a version base (/design-release-2.1, /design-release-2 or /testing) is never prefixed again, so DR2.1 links to another version are left as they are.

When DR2.1 renders a page, it uses the page's override in app/views/design-release-2.1/ when one exists (as .html, .njk or a folder index.html), and otherwise falls back to the root view of the same name. Layouts, partials and govuk or moj templates are never swapped this way.

DR2.1 pages are also treated as design release 2 pages: every DR2.1 render has isDesignRelease2Version and isDesignRelease21Version set, and the session check for design release 2 is true for DR2.1 sessions, so design release 2 behaviour applies under /design-release-2.1 unless a DR2.1 branch overrides it.
Every DR2.1 page has journeyBasePath set to /design-release-2.1, which partials use to build version-local links.

In DR2.1 the service navigation links are: Dashboard to /design-release-2.1, the service name and header home link to /design-release-2.1/index, Templates to /design-release-2.1/templates and Address book to /design-release-2.1/address-book.
The service is called "Import notification service" and uses GOV.UK service navigation.
claims.ref: app/config.json:2-4 (read by layouts/main.html as serviceName and useServiceNavigation)

claims.statement: Every page shows the GOV.UK header whose GOV.UK logo links to the service index (in DR2.1, /design-release-2.1/index); with service navigation on, the service name is shown in the service navigation bar, not in the header.
claims.quote:
homepageUrl: navServiceHref,
      serviceName: serviceName if not useServiceNavigation,

claims.statement: In DR2.1 the service navigation bar shows the service name, linking to the service index, followed by four items in this order: Dashboard, Templates, Address book, Manage account.
In DR2.1 the service navigation has no Log out item, unlike design release 2 which shows Log out after Manage account.
claims.note: Inferred by comparing the DR2.1 branch (lines 72-98, four items) with the design release 2 branch (lines 100-130, which adds "Log out").

The Manage account navigation item links nowhere (#), because no manage account href is set for DR2.1.

claims.statement: Journey pages use a two-thirds width column layout.
When the notification being edited has the status Amend, every journey page includes the cancel amendment confirmation dialog.
The cancel amendment dialog asks "Are you sure you want to cancel this amendment?".
claims.quote: Are you sure you want to cancel this amendment?

claims.statement: The cancel amendment dialog's primary button "Yes, cancel amendment" goes to /design-release-2.1/notifications/cancel-amend in DR2.1 (or to cancelAmendHref when a page sets one).
claims.quote: Yes, cancel amendment

claims.statement: The cancel amendment dialog has a "Go back" link-styled button and a Close button (labelled "Close" for screen readers); both, and clicking the overlay, dismiss the dialog without cancelling.
claims.quote:
<button class="govuk-link app-dr2-amend-modal__back-link" type="button" data-modal-dismiss>
          Go back
        </button>

claims.statement: The cancel amendment dialog is a modal dialog, hidden until opened, with aria-modal set and its heading as its accessible label.
The service index page (/index) has the page title "Import notification service", caption "Prototypes" and heading "Import notification service".
The service index introduction reads "Choose a prototype version to work on. Each version has its own journey and dashboard, with a shared address book."
claims.quote: Choose a prototype version to work on. Each version has its own journey and dashboard, with a shared address book.

claims.statement: The service index shows four release cards in this order: Design release 1, Design release 2, Design release 2.1 and Testing version; the three design releases are tagged "In design" (purple) and the testing version is tagged "Testing" (yellow). Every card has the subheading "Create a notification".

The Design release 1 card reads "The current design release journey at the root URLs. Use this for stable reference work.", has a "What the journey contains" details listing "Origin, commodity and reason for import", "Consignment, animal and arrival details", "Documents, roles and addresses" and "Review, declaration and submission", and a "Start design release 1" button to /create-notification.
claims.quote: The current design release journey at the root URLs. Use this for stable reference work.

claims.statement: The Design release 2 card reads "A duplicate of Design release 1 for making changes without affecting the original version.", its details list "Same journey as Design release 1", "Separate dashboard and session data" and "Shared address book", and its "Start design release 2" button goes to /design-release-2.
claims.quote: A duplicate of Design release 1 for making changes without affecting the original version.

claims.statement: The Design release 2.1 card reads "A duplicate of Design release 2 for making changes without affecting the original version.", its "What the journey contains" details list "Same journey as Design release 2", "Separate dashboard and session data" and "Shared address book", and its "Start design release 2.1" button goes to /design-release-2.1.
The Testing version card reads "A separate testing journey with CHEDA references and IPAFFS-style dashboard patterns." and has a "Start testing version" button to /testing, with no details section.
claims.quote: A separate testing journey with CHEDA references and IPAFFS-style dashboard patterns.

claims.statement: GET /index renders the service index page; DR2.1 has no override of it, so /design-release-2.1/index shows the same root index page with the DR2.1 navigation.
Signing in (POST /intro/sign-in) takes the user to the DR2.1 dashboard at /design-release-2.1.
The fixed design-release notification reference is GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P; the testing version uses GB.2026.7963913 - CHEDA instead.
A design-release notification reference has the form GBN-, two letters, a hyphen, two digits, a hyphen and then letters or digits (matched case-insensitively), such as GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P.

When a notification has no reference, or its reference is not in the design-release format, a new reference GBN-AG-26- followed by six random upper-case letters or digits is generated, avoiding the fixed reference and every reference already used on the dashboard, in drafts and in submitted notifications.
claims.note: The generator's body sits in another part's range; it builds `GBN-AG-26-${code}` from a six-character random code and skips any reference in the existing set.

claims.statement: Seed dashboard notifications whose reference is in the testing format are shown with a design-release reference: the first notification, and any with sequence 7963913, show GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P; others show GBN-AG-26- followed by a six-character code derived from their sequence number.

Starting a new notification journey clears every answer in the version's session, but keeps the added address book addresses, draft notifications, deleted notification references, submitted notifications, saved templates and deleted template ids, along with the testing, design release 2 and design release 2.1 session nests.

The journey session is reset when the user starts a notification at /create-notification, among other entry points (called at app/routes.js 5876, 8539, 8562, 8596, 8961, 8992, 9012, 11109, 11602 and 12107).
claims.note: The other call sites belong to other parts' pages (templates, copy, amend, dashboard); they are listed so the reconciler can find them.

claims.statement: The prototype shortcut /prototype/reason-for-import seeds a notification (origin France, no region of origin, commodity Cattle 0102, species cattle-bison-bison with 5 animals, certification purpose Slaughter, unweaned animals No, a design-release reference) and goes straight to the reason for import page.
claims.note: A designer shortcut, not a user-facing page; /prototype/reason-for-import is a DR2.1 journey prefix so it stays inside the version.

claims.statement: A page is treated as reached from the notification overview (hub) when its query or form carries from=hub.
A page is treated as reached from the check-your-answers review page when its query or form carries from=review.
A page is treated as reached from a template review when its query or form carries from=template-review, or the session is marked as editing a template from its review.

The return path to a template review is /templates/<template id> (the template being edited, or the session's template), or /templates when there is no template id; in DR2.1 this becomes /design-release-2.1/templates/<id>.

Saving a page while editing a template from its review saves the template, sets the success message "<template title> has been updated" (or "Template has been updated" when it has no title or name), clears the template editing state and returns to that template's review page.

A journey page's back link goes to the template review when the page was reached from a template review, to the notification overview (/notification-hub) when reached from the hub, and otherwise to the previous page in the journey.

A page reached from the check-your-answers review page does not get a back link to the review: the back-link rule only special-cases template review and hub, so from=review pages fall back to the previous journey page.
claims.note: Inferred from the absence of an isFromReview branch in getJourneyBackLink; individual pages may override their own back link.

claims.statement: The journey step order starts with origin of the import, what are you importing, reason for import and consignment details, in that order.
The animal identification details step follows consignment details only when at least one selected species has identifier fields.
The additional animal details step comes next only when that page would ask the certification purpose question or the unweaned animals question.
Arrival details is always a step, after the animal steps.
The transit countries step follows arrival details only when the means of transport is Rail or Road.
Means of transport values are normalised before the transit check: airplane and air mean Air; railway and rail mean Rail; road vehicle and road mean Road; vessel and sea mean Sea.
claims.quote:
airplane: 'Air',
  air: 'Air',
  railway: 'Rail',
  rail: 'Rail',
  'road vehicle': 'Road',
  road: 'Road',
  vessel: 'Sea',
  sea: 'Sea'

claims.statement: Transporter is always a step, after arrival details and any transit countries.
In DR2.1, the upload documents step is skipped when the user is creating a template; otherwise it follows transporter.
Roles and addresses, contact address for consignment and review notification are always steps, in that order, after documents.
In DR2.1, the declaration step after review is skipped when the user is creating a template; otherwise declaration is the last step.

The step order has no step for CPH number, permanent address, place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer or place of destination; those pages are reached from within roles and addresses or the hub, not as linear steps.
claims.note: Inferred by comparing getJourneySteps with JOURNEY_PATH_PREFIXES (app/lib/version-mount.js:11-46), which lists those paths. How they are reached is other parts' business.

claims.statement: The next page after a step is the following step in the order; after the last step, or from a page that is not a step, the next page is the notification overview (/notification-hub) unless the caller gives another fallback.
After roles and addresses, the next page is the notification overview instead of contact address for consignment when every notification hub section is already complete.
A notification is being amended when its status is exactly Amend.
Journey forms send the button pressed as the action field; hub and review are soft-save actions (save and leave the linear flow), and continue moves on.

When a journey page is saved, the notification is persisted as a draft; then the action review goes to the review page (/review-notification), the action hub goes to the notification overview (/notification-hub), and any other action goes to the next page.
When a journey page is saved while editing a template from its review, the save returns to the template review and does not persist a draft notification.

When a section page continues, it returns to the template review if reached from one, to the notification overview if reached from the hub, to the review page if reached from review, and otherwise to the next page in the journey; the template review takes precedence over hub, and hub over review.

By default a DR2.1 journey page shows a primary "Save and continue" button (action continue), a secondary "Save and return to overview" button (action hub) and a "Cancel and return to overview" link to the notification overview (/design-release-2.1/notification-hub).
A page may change the default actions: rename any of the three, hide the save and return to overview button, hide the cancel link, or point the cancel link elsewhere.
claims.quote:
{% set showHub = true if options.showHub is not defined else options.showHub %}
{% set showCancel = true if options.showCancel is not defined else options.showCancel %}

claims.statement: When a notification is being amended, a journey page shows a primary "Save and return" button (action review, going to the review page), a secondary "Save and continue" button (action continue) and a link-styled "Save and return to overview" button (action hub); there is no cancel link.

When the user is editing a template from its review, a journey page shows only a primary "Save and return" button (action continue, which returns to the template review) and a "Cancel" link to the template's page; this mode takes precedence over amend.

The template review Cancel link is built in the page as /templates/<template id> and is not prefixed with /design-release-2.1, so in DR2.1 it points at the root templates path rather than the version's.
claims.note: Inferred: version prefixing applies to redirects and render data, not to hrefs built inside a template. Possibly a prototype defect; the cancel href for the default mode uses journeyBasePath and is prefixed.

claims.statement: Every journey page shows a notification status bar with a status tag and the notification reference: the status is Template (with the template name instead of a reference) while creating a template, otherwise the notification's status, or Draft when it has none.
claims.quote: {% set statusText = "Template" if isCreatingTemplate else (data.notificationStatus if data.notificationStatus else "Draft") %}

claims.statement: The status tag is styled by its status name in lower case with spaces as hyphens (for example draft, amend, template), giving each status its own tag colour.
claims.note: The colours themselves live in app/assets Sass, outside the scope.

claims.statement: When the status is Amend, the status bar shows a "Cancel amend" link-styled button that opens the cancel amendment dialog.
claims.quote:
<button class="govuk-link app-dr2-notification-status__cancel-link" type="button" data-modal-open="cancel-amend-modal">
      Cancel amend
    </button>

claims.statement: The root notification status partial renders the same design release status bar under DR2.1 (as DR2.1 is also design release 2); only outside design release 2 does it fall back to GOV.UK tags coloured grey for Template, blue for Draft and purple otherwise.
claims.quote: classes: "govuk-tag--grey" if isCreatingTemplate else ("govuk-tag--blue" if statusText == "Draft" else "govuk-tag--purple")

claims.statement: Under DR2.1 the address book is reached at /design-release-2.1/address-book, and address book links built by handlers use that base followed by the page suffix or query string.
Under DR2.1 the back link to the dashboard goes to /design-release-2.1 (the testing version goes to /testing, design release 2 to /design-release-2 and the root journey to /).
The dashboard is the DR2.1 home: the version base path /design-release-2.1 is the Dashboard navigation target and the dashboard back-link target.
claims.note: What GET / renders under DR2.1 is the dashboard part's to claim; this records only that the base path is used as the dashboard link.

claims.statement: The prototype defines no custom Nunjucks filters and no default session data.
The source does not say what the Manage account or Log out pages should be in DR2.1; the scope expects the service shell, and the only account link has no destination.
claims.note: Looked in the layout, the DR2.1 version locals and the routes.js ranges of this part; no manage-account or sign-out route or href exists.

claims.statement: The source gives no page title (browser tab title) pattern for DR2.1 journey pages in the layouts; only the index page sets one.
claims.note: Each page may set its own pageTitle block; the layouts in this part define none.
